meta.title: Nicolás Amorosi, full-stack engineer
meta.description: Full-stack engineer (TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL). I build and modernize business systems end to end, from the legacy database to production. Remote from Argentina; English, Spanish, Italian.

hero.intro: Full-stack engineer. I build the systems organizations run on — academic records, HR, accounts payable — end to end, from the legacy database to production. Remote from Argentina, working in English, Spanish and Italian.
hero.status: Open to full-time remote roles. Contracts too.

about.title: About
about.p1: I studied at Universidad Adventista del Plata — Systems Analyst in 2022, Systems Engineer in 2024 — and wrote my first production code there, upgrading the university’s Rails applications.
about.p2: In 2025 I moved to Rome to run IT and development at HopeMedia Italia, the media centre of the Italian Adventist Church Union. Since August 2026 I work remotely from Entre Ríos, Argentina, for clients in Italy and Argentina. I’m an Italian citizen.
about.p3: Off the clock I fly FPV drones and keep a repair log for each one, go running, self-host a home server, and I’m building an ESP32 rack that waters balcony plants on its own.

case.privacy: The code belongs to the client and stays private. Figures are illustrations with sample data; no real records appear on this page.

scopes.caption: One request for grades, answered for three people. The scope becomes a database filter; grades outside it never leave the server.

encoding.caption: The same bytes through three decoders. UTF-8 fails loudly, latin1 fails silently, Windows-1252 gets it right.

approval.caption: Built at submission time by walking up the hierarchy. Each step keeps a snapshot of its approver, so a reorganization never rewrites past approvals.
approval.effectNote: Approved absences become entries in the monthly report

archaeology.caption: From opaque sources to a map, then to a new database — without ever touching production.

projection.caption: The projection window only renders the last output it received, so it can always be rebuilt. Slides take a detour through LibreOffice and pdf.js.

projection.mainNote: Owns state and SQLite; replays the last output
projection.screenNote: A pure function of the last output
